techniques.name: Outcome independence
techniques.summary: Caring about the person and the moment while not needing a particular result from the interaction.
techniques.how_to_apply: Set the goal as 'enjoy this and be myself' before the conversation; treat a no or a lukewarm response as information, not a verdict.
techniques.drill: Before each social event write one process goal (e.g. 'three follow-up questions') and score only that afterwards.

techniques.name: Spot and drop covert contracts
techniques.summary: Noticing when niceness is secretly a trade (I'll be lovely, so you'll like me) and replacing it with open requests and honest giving.
techniques.how_to_apply: Before a favour, compliment or agreement, ask: would I do this if it earned nothing? If not, either ask directly for what you want or don't do it.
techniques.drill: For one week, log each time you did something hoping for a hidden payoff; for each, write the direct ask you could have made.

techniques.name: Say your real opinion
techniques.summary: Sharing genuine preferences and disagreements instead of mirroring what you think she wants.
techniques.how_to_apply: When asked what you think, answer with your actual view in one sentence, then ask hers; disagree warmly when you disagree.
techniques.drill: In three conversations, state one mild, genuine disagreement and keep it friendly; note her reaction.

techniques.name: Stop approval-seeking tags
techniques.summary: Removing verbal habits that ask for reassurance, like 'is that weird?', 'does that make sense?' and 'sorry, I'm rambling'.
techniques.how_to_apply: End points with a full stop and a pause instead of a check-in; let her respond on her own.
techniques.drill: Record a 2-minute story; tally every reassurance tag; redo with zero and compare.

techniques.name: Purpose first
techniques.summary: Building a life organised around a mission he cares about, so a woman joins his world rather than becoming its centre.
techniques.how_to_apply: Keep commitments to your own projects even when dating is going well; talk about what you're building with genuine energy.
techniques.drill: Write one paragraph on what you're building this year; practise saying the 20-second version with energy.

sources.where: women as part of a full life

techniques.name: Don't make her the mission
techniques.summary: Avoiding pedestalising: treating one woman as the prize or main life goal before you know her.
techniques.how_to_apply: Keep investment in step with what you actually know about her; keep friends, hobbies and plans intact in the early weeks.
techniques.drill: After a good date, list three non-dating things you'll do that week and do them.

sources.where: don't put her first too early

techniques.name: Selective, specific interest
techniques.summary: Showing interest in her in particular, rather than being enthusiastic about everyone, which research links to being desired back.
techniques.how_to_apply: Compliment and ask about specific things she said or chose; don't gush generically.
techniques.drill: After each interaction write one specific thing you liked; say that kind of thing next time.

techniques.name: Honest expression of interest
techniques.summary: Telling her plainly that you're attracted or want to see her again, accepting the risk of rejection.
techniques.how_to_apply: Once you feel it and she's engaged, say it once, warmly, without a question tag; then let her respond.
techniques.drill: In your next three dates, state your interest once, clearly, before the end.

techniques.name: Vulnerability as a mindset
techniques.summary: Being willing to show real feelings, flaws and wants without performing; strength shown by not hiding.
techniques.how_to_apply: Share one real thing that matters to you, briefly, then return the floor; don't use vulnerability to fish for sympathy.
techniques.drill: Once per date, share one honest feeling in the moment in a single sentence.

techniques.name: Polarise rather than please
techniques.summary: Expressing your real personality so that some people like you a lot and some don't, instead of everyone feeling lukewarm.
techniques.how_to_apply: Show genuine tastes, humour and opinions early; read a mismatch as a successful filter.
techniques.drill: Name three genuine tastes you usually hide and mention one per conversation.

techniques.name: Warm-up before you go out
techniques.summary: Getting into a sociable, talkative mood before the important conversation rather than starting cold.
techniques.how_to_apply: Have a few easy chats (barista, friends) before the date or event; music and movement help.
techniques.drill: Before your next social event, have three brief friendly exchanges with strangers on the way.

techniques.name: Presence over performance
techniques.summary: Putting full attention on what's happening now rather than on planning the next line or judging yourself.
techniques.how_to_apply: When you notice yourself rehearsing, return attention to her words, her face, the setting; respond to what's actually said.
techniques.drill: During one conversation, do a 1-second body check (feet, breath) whenever you catch yourself rehearsing.

techniques.name: Counter the liking gap
techniques.summary: Remembering that people usually like us more than we think after a conversation, so pessimism fuels needy behaviour.
techniques.how_to_apply: When you leave thinking it went badly, look for her objective engagement signals before concluding anything.
techniques.drill: After each recorded chat, rate how much she liked you (1-10) before the coach review, then compare to her engagement markers.

techniques.name: Rejection reframe
techniques.summary: Treating rejection as a sign you took a risk and a filter for fit, not as evidence of low worth.
techniques.how_to_apply: After a no, say something gracious, leave, and note what you'd keep doing; never argue or sulk.
techniques.drill: Collect three small rejections this month (ask for small favours or numbers) and practise the gracious exit.

techniques.name: Hold your frame without arguing
techniques.summary: Keeping your own calm reading of a situation when she challenges it, without needing her to agree.
techniques.how_to_apply: Restate your view briefly and good-humouredly once; don't stack justifications; move on.
techniques.drill: When challenged in low-stakes chats, answer in one sentence max, then ask a question.

techniques.name: Don't over-explain
techniques.summary: Cutting long justifications, which signal you need her approval of your choices.
techniques.how_to_apply: Give the reason in one clause or none; let silence do the rest.
techniques.drill: Answer five 'why' questions about your life in one sentence each; record and check.

techniques.name: Agree and amplify
techniques.summary: Responding to a playful jab by agreeing and exaggerating it until it's absurd, which shows it didn't land.
techniques.how_to_apply: Take the accusation, inflate it humorously, smile, move on.
techniques.drill: Have a friend throw ten mock-accusations; answer each with agree-and-amplify, then with a sincere answer.

techniques.name: Sincere answer to sincere question
techniques.summary: Recognising when a 'test' is a real question about safety or values and answering it straight.
techniques.how_to_apply: If she asks about intentions, exes or safety, give a short honest answer without jokes.
techniques.drill: List three questions women often ask on early dates; write a one-line honest answer for each.

techniques.name: Pass the 'are you rattled?' check
techniques.summary: Staying relaxed when she teases or provokes, which practitioners say is the actual point of many tests.
techniques.how_to_apply: Don't flinch, don't sulk, don't overreact; a smile, a light line or a calm plain statement all pass.
techniques.drill: Notice the next three times you're teased; respond within two seconds with something light.

techniques.name: Reframe awkwardness as shared fun
techniques.summary: Turning an awkward moment into an in-joke, which removes its sting for both people.
techniques.how_to_apply: Name it lightly and make it 'ours'.
techniques.drill: In a week of chats, find two small awkward moments and name them out loud playfully.

techniques.name: Reframe the role: you're choosing too
techniques.summary: Shifting your internal frame from 'auditioning for her' to 'two people seeing if they fit'.
techniques.how_to_apply: Ask yourself during the date what you're learning about her values and whether you like them.
techniques.drill: Write three qualities you want in a partner; listen for evidence of them on your next date.

techniques.name: Slow down under pressure
techniques.summary: Deliberately lowering pace and pitch when stakes rise, countering the stress pattern of speeding up and pitching higher.
techniques.how_to_apply: When you notice adrenaline, breathe out, slow your next sentence and land it with a falling ending.
techniques.drill: Record yourself telling the same story relaxed and then while standing in front of a friend; compare rate and pitch.

techniques.name: Comfortable silence
techniques.summary: Letting a pause sit for a couple of seconds without rushing to fill it.
techniques.how_to_apply: In lulls, count to two silently, smile, then say something light or ask a real question.
techniques.drill: In low-stakes chats, let one pause run to a slow count of three before you speak.

techniques.name: Amused tolerance
techniques.summary: Meeting friction, provocation or drama with warm amusement rather than anger or anxiety.
techniques.how_to_apply: Smile through it, keep tone warm, respond with lightness, and don't escalate.
techniques.drill: When you feel irritated in a conversation this week, choose one amused response before reacting.

sources.where: humour and love in the face of her tests

techniques.name: Keep your plans
techniques.summary: Not cancelling commitments or bending boundaries at the first sign of interest from her.
techniques.how_to_apply: Offer alternatives instead of dropping what you had planned.
techniques.drill: Next time someone asks for your time when you're busy, offer an alternative rather than cancelling.

techniques.name: Don't react to bait
techniques.summary: Choosing not to take the hook when someone (including other men) tries to provoke or one-up you.
techniques.how_to_apply: Acknowledge lightly or ignore; redirect to the group or to her.
techniques.drill: When someone tries to one-up you this week, respond with genuine interest in their story instead.

techniques.name: Cocky-funny
techniques.summary: Combining exaggerated self-confidence with humour so it's obviously a joke, signalling ease without real arrogance.
techniques.how_to_apply: Say a cheeky, over-the-top line about yourself or the situation with a smile; keep the target safe and the warmth obvious.
techniques.drill: Write five over-the-top lines about your own charm; deliver each with a deadpan then a smile; keep the two that make friends laugh.

techniques.name: Mock accusation
techniques.summary: Playfully accusing her of something absurd (e.g. trying to seduce you, being a troublemaker) to create a fun dynamic.
techniques.how_to_apply: Pick a harmless, obviously untrue 'accusation' linked to something she just did; smile.
techniques.drill: Use one mock accusation per conversation for a week; note when it lands and when it doesn't.

techniques.name: Role reversal
techniques.summary: Playfully treating yourself as the one being pursued or needing to be won over.
techniques.how_to_apply: Flip the usual script with a smile: you're the one being careful with her, she has to behave.
techniques.drill: Write three role-reversal lines for common moments (she pays a compliment, she suggests a drink, she touches your arm).

techniques.name: Tease the safe stuff
techniques.summary: Teasing her about choices she's proud of or neutral things (her drink, her strong opinions), never insecurities.
techniques.how_to_apply: Tease, smile, and land on warmth within a turn or two.
techniques.drill: For each tease you make this week, add a warm line within your next turn.

techniques.name: Tease back when teased
techniques.summary: Matching her playful challenges with your own, so the banter becomes two-way.
techniques.how_to_apply: Accept her jab with a smile and return one in the same register.
techniques.drill: In banter, aim for at least two back-and-forth exchanges before shifting to sincere.

techniques.name: Tease, then sincere
techniques.summary: Alternating playful teasing with genuine appreciation so she knows the fun comes from liking her.
techniques.how_to_apply: After a run of banter, say one sincere specific compliment or ask a real question.
techniques.drill: Practise 'three jokes, one sincere' in a conversation and note how she responds to the sincere beat.

techniques.name: Role-play premise
techniques.summary: Inventing a playful fictional scenario about the two of you, which builds 'we' and fun.
techniques.how_to_apply: Take a detail and spin it into a mini-scenario; invite her to add to it.
techniques.drill: Pick three ordinary situations (queue, cooking, travel) and write one absurd 'us' premise for each.

techniques.name: Yes-and her bits
techniques.summary: Building on her joke rather than topping it with an unrelated one, the improv rule that creates co-created humour.
techniques.how_to_apply: When she says something playful, accept and extend it in the same direction.
techniques.drill: Count yes-and builds per conversation; aim to raise the number each week.

techniques.name: Playful misinterpretation
techniques.summary: Deliberately reading her innocent words as flirtatious or ridiculous, as an obvious joke.
techniques.how_to_apply: Pick up a double meaning, twist it lightly, then let it go.
techniques.drill: Listen for one ambiguous phrase per conversation and twist it lightly.

techniques.name: Callback humour
techniques.summary: Bringing back an earlier detail or joke later, which shows attention and creates in-jokes.
techniques.how_to_apply: Note one funny or distinctive detail early; reuse it once or twice later.
techniques.drill: Note one detail in the first five minutes and call back to it later; review if it landed.

techniques.name: Nicknames and in-jokes
techniques.summary: Giving a playful, affectionate nickname based on something she said, creating a private shared world.
techniques.how_to_apply: Use a nickname tied to a specific moment, only if she responds warmly.
techniques.drill: Try one moment-based nickname on a playful date; drop it if she doesn't smile.

techniques.name: Entertain yourself
techniques.summary: Saying things because they amuse you, not to get a reaction, which makes humour feel effortless.
techniques.how_to_apply: Follow your curiosity and comedic instinct; don't check her face after every line.
techniques.drill: On your next outing, say one thing purely because it amuses you, then let it go whatever her reaction.

techniques.name: Laugh off a missed joke
techniques.summary: Handling a joke that flops by acknowledging it lightly and moving on.
techniques.how_to_apply: Name it in under five words, smile, carry on.
techniques.drill: Deliberately tell a terrible pun to a friend and practise the five-word recovery.

techniques.name: Light challenge
techniques.summary: Playfully challenging her to earn your interest, e.g. questioning whether she's adventurous enough.
techniques.how_to_apply: Frame the challenge as a game with a smile, about an activity or taste, never her worth.
techniques.drill: Write three playful 'can we be friends?' challenges about tastes; use one per date.

techniques.name: Exaggeration
techniques.summary: Inflating small things to absurd proportions for comic effect.
techniques.how_to_apply: Take a mundane fact and treat it as epic.
techniques.drill: Retell three boring facts about your week with one absurd exaggeration each.

techniques.name: Self-deprecation only from strength
techniques.summary: Using self-deprecating humour sparingly and about trivial things, since it helps mainly when status is already clear.
techniques.how_to_apply: Joke about small foibles, not core worth; keep it rare.
techniques.drill: Audit a recording for self-deprecation; keep at most one trivial one.

techniques.name: Tease the situation, not the person
techniques.summary: Directing humour at the setting, the moment or shared absurdities, a lower-risk way to be playful.
techniques.how_to_apply: Comment wryly on the venue, the queue or the music.
techniques.drill: Make one observational joke about the setting in the first two minutes of each conversation.

techniques.name: Slow, unhurried delivery
techniques.summary: Speaking at a relaxed, steady pace that suggests you're not worried about losing her attention.
techniques.how_to_apply: Slightly slower than your nervous pace; pause between ideas; don't rush endings.
techniques.drill: Read a paragraph aloud at your normal pace, then with a breath after each sentence; compare.

techniques.name: Pause before the point
techniques.summary: A short pause before a key line, which adds weight and draws attention.
techniques.how_to_apply: Take a beat before punchlines, compliments and invitations.
techniques.drill: Mark three pause points in a story and practise hitting them.

techniques.name: Land statements with a downward inflection
techniques.summary: Ending statements on a falling pitch so they sound decided rather than asked.
techniques.how_to_apply: Drop your pitch on the last stressed word; stop talking.
techniques.drill: Full-stop drill: five opinions, each with a clear fall and a one-second silence.

techniques.name: Replace fillers with silence
techniques.summary: Swapping 'um', 'like' and 'you know' for brief silent pauses.
techniques.how_to_apply: When you feel a filler coming, close your mouth and pause.
techniques.drill: Two-minute story drill: every filler replaced by silence; check fillers_per_100w.

techniques.name: Cut hedges from opinions
techniques.summary: Removing 'maybe', 'sort of', 'I guess' from opinions and plans, while keeping honest uncertainty when it's real.
techniques.how_to_apply: State the view plainly; if unsure, say 'my guess is' once rather than scattering hedges.
techniques.drill: Rewrite five of your recent text messages without hedges; read them aloud.

techniques.name: Vocal variety in stories
techniques.summary: Using a wider range of pitch, pace and volume when telling stories, which reads as charismatic.
techniques.how_to_apply: Lift energy in the exciting part, drop low and slow for the punchline or the personal bit.
techniques.drill: Tell the same 60-second story flat, then with deliberate variation; compare pitch_range_st.

techniques.name: Lower, softer voice for intimacy
techniques.summary: Dropping volume and slowing down when the conversation turns personal or flirtatious.
techniques.how_to_apply: When she shares something personal or you compliment her, lower volume and slow down.
techniques.drill: Practise one sincere compliment at normal volume then at 70%; ask a friend which felt warmer.

techniques.name: Warm tone: smile in the voice
techniques.summary: Letting warmth be audible (smiling while speaking, relaxed breath), balancing strength with friendliness.
techniques.how_to_apply: Smile slightly while greeting and asking questions; relax your jaw.
techniques.drill: Record a greeting neutral and with a smile; listen for the difference.

techniques.name: Hold the floor gracefully
techniques.summary: Finishing your thought when lightly interrupted rather than immediately giving up the turn.
techniques.how_to_apply: Raise a hand or say 'one sec' and finish briefly; then hand over with a question.
techniques.drill: In group chats, finish one interrupted thought per evening, then hand over.

techniques.name: Project to be heard
techniques.summary: Speaking loudly enough for the setting, as quiet mumbled speech signals low confidence in noisy venues.
techniques.how_to_apply: Speak from the chest, aim your voice at her, adjust up in bars.
techniques.drill: Count how many times you're asked to repeat yourself in a loud venue; aim for zero.

techniques.name: Full attention, quick fitting responses
techniques.summary: Responding promptly and on-topic, which signals engagement; fast, fitting replies track 'clicking'.
techniques.how_to_apply: Listen fully; let your reply come from what she said, not a prepared line.
techniques.drill: In one conversation, make every reply begin with a word she just used.

techniques.name: Don't rush to answer compliments or questions
techniques.summary: Taking a breath before answering charged questions or compliments, rather than rushing to deflect.
techniques.how_to_apply: Accept a compliment with 'thank you' and a pause; answer personal questions after a beat.
techniques.drill: Accept the next five compliments you get with only 'thank you' and a smile.

techniques.name: Decisive yes/no answers
techniques.summary: Answering simple questions directly instead of with waffling.
techniques.how_to_apply: Lead with yes, no or a choice; add reason only if needed.
techniques.drill: For a day, answer every simple preference question with a choice in the first word.

techniques.name: Presence-power-warmth balance
techniques.summary: Charisma as a mix of presence (attention), power (capability) and warmth (goodwill); missing one makes the others read worse.
techniques.how_to_apply: Check each conversation: was I present, did I sound capable, did I sound kind?
techniques.drill: After each recording, score yourself 1-5 on presence, power and warmth; compare with the coach's read.

techniques.name: Hook, tension, payoff
techniques.summary: Telling stories with a clear opening hook, a moment of tension and a payoff, which research links to men's attractiveness and status.
techniques.how_to_apply: Open with the most intriguing line, build to one obstacle, deliver the payoff, stop.
techniques.drill: Write your three best stories as hook / tension / payoff in three lines each; tell each in under 90 seconds.

techniques.name: Keep it short
techniques.summary: Trimming stories to their essential beats so the other person stays engaged and gets a turn.
techniques.how_to_apply: Aim for under about 90 seconds (heuristic); cut background she doesn't need.
techniques.drill: Time your go-to story; cut it by a third without losing the payoff.

techniques.name: Paint the scene
techniques.summary: Using concrete images, dialogue and feelings so she can picture the moment.
techniques.how_to_apply: Include one sensory detail and one line of dialogue in each story.
techniques.drill: Retell yesterday as a story with one smell, one sound and one quote.

techniques.name: Demonstrate, don't declare
techniques.summary: Letting qualities like competence, courage or kindness come out through what happened, not by stating them.
techniques.how_to_apply: Choose stories where the trait is visible in your actions; never add 'I'm a pretty adventurous guy'.
techniques.drill: Rewrite one 'I'm the kind of guy who...' claim as a 20-second story.

techniques.name: Character over credentials
techniques.summary: Choosing stories that reveal values and emotions (curiosity, loyalty, fear overcome) rather than income or achievements.
techniques.how_to_apply: Pick stories where something mattered to you emotionally.
techniques.drill: List five stories; mark each as 'credential' or 'character'; lead with character ones.

sources.where: women connect with appreciation and focus on them

techniques.name: Match and step up disclosure
techniques.summary: Sharing personal information at roughly the same depth as her, then going slightly deeper, which builds closeness.
techniques.how_to_apply: After she shares, share something comparable; occasionally go one notch deeper.
techniques.drill: Practise the Aron-style progression with a friend: three question sets of increasing depth.

techniques.name: Stories that invite hers
techniques.summary: Ending a story with a hook that naturally invites her to share a similar experience.
techniques.how_to_apply: Finish with a beat or a light question tied to the theme.
techniques.drill: Add a natural invitation to the end of each of your three best stories.

techniques.name: Use 'you' and 'we' in stories
techniques.summary: Pulling her into the story by relating it to her or to an imagined shared future.
techniques.how_to_apply: Connect a story to something she said, or end with 'we should...'.
techniques.drill: For one story, add a line that links it to her.

techniques.name: Open threads in stories
techniques.summary: Leaving interesting loose details she can ask about, which hands her easy ways in.
techniques.how_to_apply: Mention a curious detail without explaining it fully.
techniques.drill: Drop one unexplained interesting detail per conversation and see if she picks it up.

techniques.name: Avoid humblebrags
techniques.summary: Not dressing up boasts as complaints, which lowers liking more than straight bragging.
techniques.how_to_apply: Either state the fact plainly when relevant or leave it out.
techniques.drill: Scan a recording for humblebrags; restate any as plain facts.

techniques.name: Follow-up questions
techniques.summary: Asking questions that build on what she just said; the strongest research-backed liking behaviour in early conversations.
techniques.how_to_apply: Take a word from her answer and ask about it, two levels deep before switching topic.
techniques.drill: Two-deep rule: two follow-ups on any interesting answer before changing topic.

techniques.name: Statements instead of questions
techniques.summary: Making observations or guesses about her instead of asking interview questions, which creates more engaging conversation.
techniques.how_to_apply: Turn 'where are you from?' into a guess: 'You seem like you grew up by the sea.'
techniques.drill: Convert five standard first-date questions into playful statements.

techniques.name: Playful cold read
techniques.summary: Making a perceptive but general guess about her personality; it often feels accurate because of the Barnum effect.
techniques.how_to_apply: Base it on something she actually said; frame it as a guess; be curious if wrong.
techniques.drill: Practise three reads on friends from observed details only; note accuracy.

techniques.name: Label the feeling
techniques.summary: Naming the emotion behind what she's describing, which shows understanding.
techniques.how_to_apply: Use 'sounds like...' or 'seems like...' plus the feeling, then pause.
techniques.drill: In three conversations, make one emotional label each and note her response.

techniques.name: Appreciation and sympathy
techniques.summary: Specific appreciation ('that's brilliant') and sympathy ('that must have been hard') made women feel connected in speed-date research.
techniques.how_to_apply: Respond to good news with specific appreciation and to hard news with sympathy before moving on.
techniques.drill: Replace every 'cool' in a conversation with a specific reaction.

techniques.name: Collaborative completion
techniques.summary: Briefly finishing or adding to her sentence to show you're following, which signalled understanding in speed dates.
techniques.how_to_apply: Use sparingly when you clearly get where she's going.
techniques.drill: Listen for one moment per chat where a short completion fits.

techniques.name: Threading
techniques.summary: Picking one of several hooks in her answer to continue, so the conversation never hits a dead end.
techniques.how_to_apply: Listen for 2-3 hooks in each answer; follow the most emotional or unusual one.
techniques.drill: Listen to a podcast interview; pause after each answer and list three hooks.

techniques.name: Go from facts to feelings
techniques.summary: Shifting questions from what she does to why, how it felt and what she wants.
techniques.how_to_apply: After a fact, ask about the motivation or emotion behind it.
techniques.drill: For each fact she gives, ask one 'why' or 'what was that like'.

sources.where: deeper conversations less awkward than expected

techniques.name: Deep but light questions
techniques.summary: Asking more interesting questions than small talk, delivered playfully, since people underestimate how much strangers enjoy depth.
techniques.how_to_apply: Swap 'what do you do?' for 'what are you excited about at the moment?'
techniques.drill: Prepare five 'deep but light' questions and rotate them.

techniques.name: Language and energy matching
techniques.summary: Converging with her style of speech, energy and vocabulary; style matching predicts relationship initiation.
techniques.how_to_apply: Notice her pace, energy and favourite words; meet her nearer to them.
techniques.drill: Review a recording: where did your energies diverge? Practise one adjustment.

techniques.name: Mirror her last words
techniques.summary: Repeating the last few key words she said with a curious tone, prompting her to expand.
techniques.how_to_apply: Repeat 1-3 words, slight upward tone, then wait.
techniques.drill: Use three mirrors in a low-stakes chat; count how long she talks after each.

techniques.name: Focus the conversation on her
techniques.summary: Keeping much of the topical focus on her life and views; both sexes reported more 'click' when talk centred on the woman.
techniques.how_to_apply: Return the spotlight to her after your stories; don't let it drift into your résumé.
techniques.drill: Review a recording and mark whose life each topic was about.

sources.where: talk in terms of their interests

techniques.name: Don't make her carry it
techniques.summary: Taking responsibility for keeping conversation flowing so she isn't forced to ask all the questions.
techniques.how_to_apply: If she's asked two questions in a row, ask one back or offer a story.
techniques.drill: Track the question ratio in your next three recordings.

sources.where: women disconnected when they had to ask

techniques.name: Use her name and specifics
techniques.summary: Using her name and specific details she shared, which makes her feel noticed.
techniques.how_to_apply: Use her name once or twice; refer back to specifics.
techniques.drill: Use the name of three new people in conversation this week.

techniques.name: Ask about her passions
techniques.summary: Steering towards what lights her up, so her emotional state during the conversation is positive and associated with you.
techniques.how_to_apply: Listen for energy spikes in her voice and ask more there.
techniques.drill: In a recording, find her highest-energy moment and note whether you followed it.

techniques.name: Find commonalities, then differ playfully
techniques.summary: Building rapport through genuine shared interests, then adding contrast so it isn't bland agreement.
techniques.how_to_apply: Note a real shared thing; enjoy it; then playfully disagree on a detail.
techniques.drill: Look for one genuine commonality and one playful disagreement per date.

techniques.name: Validate before disagreeing
techniques.summary: Acknowledging her perspective before offering a different one, keeping warmth and frame.
techniques.how_to_apply: 'I see why you'd think that' then your view.
techniques.drill: In the next disagreement, validate first in one sentence.

techniques.name: Make intent clear
techniques.summary: Signalling romantic rather than friendly interest so you don't drift into the friend zone and she can respond honestly.
techniques.how_to_apply: Once rapport is there, say something clearly romantic once, warmly, and see how she responds.
techniques.drill: In your next date, say one clearly romantic line before the halfway point.

sources.where: women want men to show interest

techniques.name: Specific compliment on character
techniques.summary: One sincere compliment about something she chose (a story, a view, her style), said once and left alone.
techniques.how_to_apply: Make it specific, say it calmly, don't wait for a reaction.
techniques.drill: One specific choice-based compliment per date, then drop it.

techniques.name: Escalate in step with her
techniques.summary: Gradually moving to more personal and flirtatious topics only after signs she's enjoying it.
techniques.how_to_apply: After each step, read her next three turns; continue if she matches, step back if she pulls away.
techniques.drill: After each escalation, check her next three turns in the recording.

techniques.name: Flirty subtext, not explicit content
techniques.summary: Letting flirtation live in implication and playfulness rather than explicit sexual talk early on.
techniques.how_to_apply: Hint, imply, let her fill the gap; keep it deniable and light.
techniques.drill: Rewrite three blunt flirty lines as subtext.

techniques.name: Tension and release
techniques.summary: Alternating playful challenge or teasing with warmth, giving the conversation emotional rhythm.
techniques.how_to_apply: After a playful jab or disagreement, follow with appreciation; keep both honest.
techniques.drill: Write five lines that pair a playful challenge with a compliment.

techniques.name: Let tension sit
techniques.summary: Not defusing every charged moment with a joke or nervous chatter.
techniques.how_to_apply: When a moment feels charged, hold it for a beat before speaking.
techniques.drill: Next charged moment, count one breath before responding.

techniques.name: Keep your edges
techniques.summary: Maintaining your own views and direction rather than merging into constant agreement; difference keeps attraction alive.
techniques.how_to_apply: Disagree warmly, keep your own interests visible, don't mirror everything she says.
techniques.drill: Notice your agreement rate in a recording; aim for honest agreement only.

techniques.name: Keep some mystery
techniques.summary: Not revealing everything at once; letting her discover you over time.
techniques.how_to_apply: Answer honestly but not exhaustively; leave some stories for later.
techniques.drill: Pick one good story you'll save for a later date.

techniques.name: Future projection
techniques.summary: Playfully imagining future shared scenarios, which builds 'we' and romantic frame.
techniques.how_to_apply: Light, obviously playful 'we' futures, not commitment talk.
techniques.drill: Use one playful future projection on your next date.

techniques.name: Express attraction directly and calmly
techniques.summary: Saying you find her attractive in a relaxed, specific way, rather than hiding behind jokes.
techniques.how_to_apply: Say it once, calmly, without asking for a response.
techniques.drill: Practise one calm, direct compliment with a friend until it feels natural.

techniques.name: Playful disqualification
techniques.summary: Joking that you two could never work, which creates playful tension when interest is already clear.
techniques.how_to_apply: Use only when rapport and mutual interest are obvious; keep it absurd.
techniques.drill: Pair a playful disqualification with a warm comment.

techniques.name: Desire needs separateness (long-term)
techniques.summary: In relationships, maintaining individual lives, interests and some novelty sustains desire.
techniques.how_to_apply: Keep your own passions; talk about them with energy; plan new experiences together.
techniques.drill: Name one solo pursuit to maintain and one novel shared activity per month.

techniques.name: Default plus easy out
techniques.summary: Proposing a specific plan while giving her an easy way to decline or adjust.
techniques.how_to_apply: Name day, place and activity; add a light 'unless you'd rather...'.
techniques.drill: Phrase every suggestion this week as a concrete default with an easy exit.

techniques.name: Lead without asking permission at every step
techniques.summary: Moving things along (next topic, next drink, leaving) with light assertive statements instead of repeated check-ins.
techniques.how_to_apply: Suggest, don't poll; still read her reaction.
techniques.drill: Use 'let's' for three small decisions on your next outing.

techniques.name: Move on when energy dips
techniques.summary: Switching topic, activity or venue before the conversation goes flat.
techniques.how_to_apply: When answers shorten, change topic or suggest moving.
techniques.drill: In a recording, find the first energy dip and note how long you took to shift.

techniques.name: Smooth transitions
techniques.summary: Changing topics with a link or a light marker so it feels natural.
techniques.how_to_apply: Bridge with a word from the last topic or a playful 'random question'.
techniques.drill: Practise three bridges in a chat with a friend.

techniques.name: Choose when asked
techniques.summary: Making the choice when she says 'you pick', which takes the planning burden off her.
techniques.how_to_apply: Pick quickly and say why in a few words.
techniques.drill: Next time someone says 'you choose', decide within three seconds.

techniques.name: Ask clearly
techniques.summary: Asking for a date or number directly, without hedging or disguising it as something else.
techniques.how_to_apply: Name what you want and a plan: 'I'd like to take you out. Saturday?'
techniques.drill: End your next three good conversations with a clear ask.

techniques.name: Accept the answer gracefully
techniques.summary: Taking any answer, including no or maybe, lightly and without persuasion.
techniques.how_to_apply: Respond warmly and move on; a maybe is not a yes to chase.
techniques.drill: Role-play three declines with a friend, answering each in one gracious line.

techniques.name: End on a high
techniques.summary: Leaving or wrapping up while energy is good, rather than letting it fade.
techniques.how_to_apply: When things peak, propose the next step and wrap up.
techniques.drill: Notice the peak moment of your next date and close within 15 minutes of it.

techniques.name: Set the frame early
techniques.summary: Establishing the tone (playful, curious, warm) in the first minute, which tends to carry through.
techniques.how_to_apply: Open with an easy, positive, slightly playful line that sets the mood.
techniques.drill: Prepare three situational openers and use one per day for a week.

techniques.name: Verbal indicators of interest
techniques.summary: Recognising audible signs she's interested: her questions, longer answers, laughter, 'we' talk, her own teasing.
techniques.how_to_apply: Check these before escalating; treat them as a running total, not one signal.
techniques.drill: After each recording, estimate her interest, then compare with these counts.

techniques.name: Spot disinterest early
techniques.summary: Noticing short answers, no questions back, topic changes or attempts to leave, and stepping back.
techniques.how_to_apply: When two or more signs appear, de-escalate or offer an easy exit.
techniques.drill: Mark the moment in a recording where her engagement dropped; note your next move.

techniques.name: Respect her signals over your plan
techniques.summary: Prioritising her responses over any technique or plan; a calibrated man adjusts.
techniques.how_to_apply: If something doesn't land, drop it.
techniques.drill: Review one recording: list where you persisted with a bit that wasn't landing.

techniques.name: Match her energy level
techniques.summary: Adjusting your energy to slightly above hers, not wildly higher or lower.
techniques.how_to_apply: If she's calm, slow down; if she's lively, lift up.
techniques.drill: In a recording, compare your rate and loudness with hers in the first 5 minutes.

techniques.name: Repair a joke that offended
techniques.summary: Acknowledging quickly and sincerely when a joke hurt, without grovelling.
techniques.how_to_apply: One sincere line, then move on.
techniques.drill: Practise a one-line repair for three plausible misfires.

techniques.name: Recover from awkward silences
techniques.summary: Using a light observation or callback to restart after a lull, without panic.
techniques.how_to_apply: Have a few easy re-starters: observation, callback, playful question.
techniques.drill: Keep three re-starters in mind for your next outing.

techniques.name: Win the group
techniques.summary: Engaging her friends warmly and including everyone, rather than isolating her.
techniques.how_to_apply: Address the group first; be friendly to everyone; don't rush to separate her.
techniques.drill: In group settings, make sure each person has spoken to you at least once.

techniques.name: Include, don't compete
techniques.summary: Responding to other men in the group with friendliness rather than competing or putting them down.
techniques.how_to_apply: Be friendly, share the spotlight, praise others' stories.
techniques.drill: Praise one other person's story in your next group chat.

techniques.name: Check your read (projection bias)
techniques.summary: Knowing that people mainly project their own intentions when guessing whether someone's flirting.
techniques.how_to_apply: Check her behaviour, not your feelings, before concluding she's interested.
techniques.drill: Rate her interest before the coach review and compare with her signals.

techniques.name: Context-appropriate humour
techniques.summary: Adjusting humour type and intensity to the setting and her personality.
techniques.how_to_apply: Gentler humour with serious or reserved people; bolder in playful settings.
techniques.drill: Track which kind of humour gets laughs in which settings.

techniques.name: Offer an easy out
techniques.summary: Giving her a graceful way to end or decline, which lowers pressure and often increases comfort.
techniques.how_to_apply: Make it easy for her to leave, decline or change her mind.
techniques.drill: At each escalation point, include one easy-out phrase.

techniques.name: Prestige, not dominance
techniques.summary: Gaining status through competence, generosity and humour rather than intimidation; women in studies prefer prestige.
techniques.how_to_apply: Share expertise generously; never put others down to rise.
techniques.drill: Share one useful piece of expertise per week without being asked twice.

techniques.name: Pre-selection without bragging
techniques.summary: Being seen as socially valued (friends, warm greetings) can raise appeal; mention social life naturally, not as a boast.
techniques.how_to_apply: Mention friends and social life casually where relevant; never list women.
techniques.drill: Notice whether your stories include other people; add one where natural.

techniques.name: Screen for compatibility
techniques.summary: Asking questions that reveal her values and whether she fits what you want.
techniques.how_to_apply: Ask about things that matter to you (ambition, kindness, humour) with curiosity.
techniques.drill: Write your top three partner values and one question for each.

techniques.name: Appreciate good answers
techniques.summary: When she shows a quality you value, say so, which signals you have standards and makes her feel seen.
techniques.how_to_apply: Name the quality simply.
techniques.drill: Once per date, appreciate a quality she shows.

techniques.name: Calm boundaries
techniques.summary: Saying no or naming disrespect calmly and briefly, without lecturing or punishing.
techniques.how_to_apply: State the boundary in one sentence; move on or leave if it's crossed again.
techniques.drill: Practise three boundary sentences aloud for common situations.

techniques.name: Don't tolerate flaking or disrespect silently
techniques.summary: Responding to repeated cancellations or rudeness by lowering investment, not pleading.
techniques.how_to_apply: Respond briefly and warmly, then let her re-initiate.
techniques.drill: When someone flakes, reply once, warmly, and leave the next move to them.

techniques.name: Match her investment
techniques.summary: Keeping your effort roughly in step with hers, so you don't over-pursue.
techniques.how_to_apply: Notice who asks more questions, initiates more, compliments more.
techniques.drill: In a recording, compare your and her questions and compliments.

techniques.name: Don't over-compliment
techniques.summary: Limiting compliments so each one means something, since gushing reads as unselective.
techniques.how_to_apply: One or two specific compliments per date.
techniques.drill: Count your compliments in a recording; keep the best one or two.

techniques.name: Accept compliments simply
techniques.summary: Taking compliments with a thank you rather than deflecting or bragging.
techniques.how_to_apply: Thank you, smile, maybe return the warmth.
techniques.drill: Accept five compliments this week with just 'thank you'.

techniques.name: Plain facts, no humblebrag
techniques.summary: Stating achievements plainly when relevant, not hiding or overselling them.
techniques.how_to_apply: Say it once, matter-of-factly, then return to her.
techniques.drill: Write a one-line plain description of your work and practise it.

techniques.name: Don't seek reassurance
techniques.summary: Not asking her to confirm she's having a good time or likes you.
techniques.how_to_apply: Trust the signals; if unsure, read her behaviour.
techniques.drill: Count reassurance requests in a recording; cut to zero except genuine comfort checks.

techniques.name: Negging
techniques.summary: Backhanded compliments or mild put-downs meant to lower her confidence so she seeks your approval.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: affectionate teasing about safe topics, followed by warmth.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Disqualifying her looks
techniques.summary: Openly suggesting she's not attractive enough to interest you, to unsettle her.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: honest, selective interest.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Overriding last-minute resistance
techniques.summary: Treating her hesitation or no as something to get past.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: stop, check in, respect the answer.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Persistence after a decline
techniques.summary: Repeatedly asking or arguing after she has said no.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: accept the answer gracefully.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Pressing drinks
techniques.summary: Encouraging her to drink more to lower inhibitions.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: let her set her own pace.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Isolating her
techniques.summary: Steering her away from her friends to remove social support.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: include her friends; propose moving only with her clear yes.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Verbal escalation ignoring her cues
techniques.summary: Continuing sexual or intimate talk when she shows discomfort.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: step back at the first sign of discomfort.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: False time constraint
techniques.summary: Claiming you have to leave soon to lower her guard, without meaning it.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: be honest about your time.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Invented stories and fake personas
techniques.summary: Telling fabricated stories or claiming false credentials to impress.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: true stories told well.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Embedded commands and NLP patterns
techniques.summary: Covertly inserting suggestive phrases to influence her feelings without awareness.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: direct, honest expression.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Fake cold-read 'psychic' connection
techniques.summary: Using Barnum statements to make her believe you understand her uniquely.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: openly playful guesses.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Push-pull to unsettle
techniques.summary: Alternating approval and rejection specifically to create anxiety and chase.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: honest tension-and-release with consistent warmth.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Dread game
techniques.summary: Hinting she could lose you to other women to keep her insecure.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: secure, honest commitment and a full life of your own.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Freeze-outs and silent treatment
techniques.summary: Withdrawing warmth to punish or control.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: calm, direct boundary statements.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Manufactured jealousy plotline
techniques.summary: Deliberately triggering jealousy to raise her investment.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: natural mention of social life.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.

techniques.name: Seduction-as-strategy of creating need
techniques.summary: Greene-style steps of creating emptiness or confusion to make her dependent.
techniques.how_to_apply: Do not use. Ethical alternative: genuine connection and honesty.
techniques.drill: Coach flags it; Tom practises the ethical alternative instead.
